statement: Proving persistence inside one process proves nothing about persistence, because a TEMP table behaves identically until the process dies.

body.problem: canvas_artifacts shipped as CREATE TEMP TABLE. SQLite keeps a TEMP table only for the connection that made it, so every lesson appended to a canvas vanished when the API server stopped.
body.context: Eighteen durability laws ran on sqliteMemoryStore(':memory:') -- one connection, one process -- where TEMP and permanent are indistinguishable. A live restart proof passed because the pre-Stage-H blob was re-migrated into the empty table each time.
body.whenToUse: Whenever a claim is 'it is saved': open a real file, close the store, open a new store on the same path, and read again.
failureModes: a persistence test that uses an in-memory database
a restart proof whose success is explained by a migration path rather than by durability

evidence.symbol: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS canvas_artifacts

evidence.measurement: sqlite3 <repo>/data/canvas-memory.db 'SELECT name FROM sqlite_master' returned canvas_memory only; canvas_artifacts was absent from the file entirely. After the one-word fix: one ask produced one row within 2s, and it survived a stop/start.

falsifiedBy: A persistence guarantee that holds across a real process restart while its tests only ever use one connection.
